name: enhancer of zeste 1 polycomb repressive complex 2 subunit
pathways: negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

function.text: EZH1 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase EZH1. Annotated molecular activities include protein-lysine N-methyltransferase activity and transcription corepressor activity. It participates in negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription and negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.

function.text: EZH1 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase EZH1. It is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH1 complex, which methylates 'Lys-27' of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It is required for embryonic stem cell derivation and self-renewal, suggesting that it is involved in safeguarding embryonic stem cell identity. Compared to EZH2-containing complexes, it is less abundant in embryonic stem cells, has weak methyltransferase activity and plays a less critical role in forming H3K27me3, which is required for embryonic stem cell identity and proper differentiation.
